title: feat(spec,lint): a list-view grouping level can order its groups by another field (`grouping.fields[].orderBy`)
body:
Fixes #25786
Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: added

A list-view grouping level can now order its groups by another field of the same object: `{ field: 'period_label', orderBy: 'period_start', order: 'desc' }`. Before this, a period label grouped as text (`Nov 2026`, `Oct 2026`, `Q1 2027`, `Q4 2025`), so HotCRM's forecast list carried a second, outer grouping level on `period_start` and showed two header rows per forecast.

## What changes

- **Spec (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`).** `GroupingFieldSchema` gains `orderBy?: string`. It is optional with no default; absent, or naming the grouping field itself, means the level orders by its own key exactly as before. Its name is refused padded, as `field`'s is (#17360's ruling). The rule is a native `.regex()`, so the published JSON Schema states it as `pattern` instead of adding an `x-dropped-refinements` site.
- **Compiler (`packages/spec/src/ui/view-grouping-query.ts`).** `compileListViewGroupQuery` adds one node per ordered level, `min` over `orderBy` for `order: 'asc'` and `max` for `'desc'`, aliased by `columnSummaryAlias` (`min_period_start`). Each group sits where its first row would sit if the rows were sorted by `orderBy`.
  - The grouping key stays the only `groupBy` column, so there is still one header per label.
  - A column summary declaring the same `min` is the same node.
  - An alias landing on a grouped field's column is `alias_collision`.
  - A blank `orderBy` is `grouping_order_by_blank` (`INVALID_QUERY` / 400).
  - In a multi-level grouping the outer level folds exactly (the min of mins, the max of maxes).
  - `depth` limits the nodes to the grouped levels.
  - A new export, `listViewGroupOrderColumn(grouping, level)`, names the header-row column a level sorts by.
- **Lint (`packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`).** `grouping.fields[].orderBy` is judged the way the server judges it, on `os validate`, `os build` and the runtime view save door:
  - an unknown name is `list-view-field-unknown` (error);
  - a dotted path is `list-view-field-dotted` (error), on a new `aggregate` axis;
  - a type `min` / `max` cannot order on every backend is the new `list-view-group-order-unorderable` (error). The pair is asked of `isAggregateCompatibleWithFieldType`, as the engine's type door asks it, so the string classes (collation-dependent) and the virtual `formula` are refused, along with every other type outside the numeric, temporal and boolean classes.
  - The rule has an `os explain` entry.

## What the server needs (measured, as the order asked)

No new server code. The group sort stays the consumer's (`EngineAggregateOptions` carries no `orderBy`, and `order` was already applied by the consumer over the header rows). What the header rows lacked was the value to sort by, and the existing aggregate door already serves it:

- `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` → `protocol.findData` → `engine.aggregate` answers `min` / `max` over `date` and `datetime` operands on both tiers. That is driver-sql pushdown, and the in-memory `applyInMemoryAggregation` behind a driver that does not push down.
- The values are identical in value and `typeof` per column on both tiers, asc and desc. This is pinned in `packages/rest/src/list-view-grouping-query-door.test.ts` §11, with the tier asserted by the fork counters, not assumed.
- The door refuses what the lint refuses, `400 INVALID_FIELD`:
  - an unknown or dotted operand at `findData`'s ingress (`assertAggregationFieldsExist`);
  - an unorderable type at `engine.aggregate`'s type door.
  - §11 pins a `text` operand and a dotted `period_start.year`.
- Paged groups: the header query is compiled unpaged, so the consumer sorts the whole header set. A `limit` on the header query is sliced by `findData` in emission order before any sort, so a paged header set honours neither `order` nor `orderBy`. That is the limit already recorded on `GroupingConfigSchema` ("Header cardinality is unbounded"), unchanged here; bounding it is `orderBy` + `limit` on the aggregate verb, an engine-contract card of its own.

## Evidence

Final head `21dc9ad7`. `main` was merged twice: once before the review (`6679644a`), and again after the sibling spec card #25755 landed (`abebc4e1`). There were no conflicts, and the whole workspace was rebuilt each time (`pnpm build`, 76/76).

- Tests on the final head:
  - `@objectstack/spec`: full suite, 800 files, 23119 passed / 1 todo.
  - `@objectstack/lint`: full suite, 163 files, 7331/7331.
  - `@objectstack/rest`: `list-view-grouping-query-door.test.ts`, 53/53 (9 new in §11).
- Ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with the file restored to its HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` empty afterwards:
  - lint verdict forced silent (`|| true` on the compatibility check): 8 red;
  - compiler order nodes dropped (`...orders.slice(0, 0)`): 5 red;
  - the padded-name regex widened to `/[\s\S]*/`: 6 red.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on the final diff derived 114 commands. All 114 ran on the final head, each exit code recorded before any pipe: 114 × exit 0. `--ran` reconciles to "114 derived, 114 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
  - Two prerequisites were met first: a full `pnpm build`, and the self-test fixture commit fetched into the shallow clone.
  - Also run, all exit 0: the five roster gates whose roster sits under a path of this diff (`check-changeset-fixed`, `check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`), `check:error-code-provenance`, and `typecheck` for spec, lint and rest.
- Dogfood battery: n/a. No `!` in the title, and `Clause-②` carries no `(narrowing)` arm.

## Review

An independent full review of the whole diff (a fresh reviewer at the contract-review tier) returned CHANGES-REQUIRED with five findings. All five are fixed in `5d64c378`, `6a3bf131` and `d37faf8f`, and the delta re-review's one nit in `5df57e7f`:

- a padded `orderBy` was accepted by the schema;
- the unknown and dotted refusals were attributed to the wrong door;
- the paged-header case was not stated;
- the tie direction was unspecified;
- the refused-type list was narrower than the table.

The delta re-review verdict is posted as a comment on this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- **objectui reads nothing yet.** `orderBy` is declared and compiled, but the console grid ignores it until the objectui child lands: render the label from `field`, order the headers by `listViewGroupOrderColumn`, nulls last, ties by key in the same direction. That child card is filed in objectui with `Blocked-by:` this PR. HotCRM's one-line view edit (dropping its outer `period_start` level) comes after it, and is not this PR.
- **A dotted `grouping.fields[].field` is not judged by lint** (pinned silent in `validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts`), while the data door refuses it: `400 INVALID_FIELD`, "Unknown field 'period_start.year' … a related record's column cannot be a grouping target", measured through the §11 fixture. This predates the PR and is out of scope here; it is listed in the report.
- **`field` keeps its `superRefine` and its `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` row**, while `orderBy` publishes the same non-padded rule as a JSON Schema `pattern`. Moving `field` to the same `.regex()` would shrink the ledger, but that is a separate change.
